name: Kunsthalle Zürich
funding: Funded by members and patrons, City of Zürich and Canton Zürich subsidies, the Ernst Göhner, Foksal Gallery, Gubler Hablützel and Luma foundations, and Ringier AG.

name: Migros Museum
funding: Institution of the Migros-Kulturprozent, carried by the Migros cooperative federation, which pays a turnover-based sum into culture since 1957. The sheet lists CHF 12 tickets and no public funder.

name: National Museum of Damascus
funding: Its parent body, the Directorate-General of Antiquities and Museums, partners UNESCO's 2025 project: initial budget $175,000, no donor named. No museum budget is published.

name: Kaohsiung Museum of Fine Arts
funding: Kaohsiung City administrative corporation since 2017; 2025 donors: Applied Materials Taiwan, Rotary 3510, art foundations, shipping, King's Town Bank foundation.

name: Juming Museum
funding: Ju Ming Culture and Education Foundation (assets NT$167M, 2020), plus admissions, friends scheme and exhibition sponsors.

name: National Taiwan Museum of Fine Arts
funding: Funded by the Ministry of Culture. 2025 gifts of NT$5.64M came from property and building-materials firms, the E.SUN Foundation (bank), France's CCAC and individuals.

name: Tainan Art Museum
funding: Administrative corporation. 2025 revenue NT$201M: Tainan City subsidy NT$89.7M, Ministry of Culture and others NT$25M, tickets and parking NT$57M, donations NT$3.7M.

name: Hong-gah Museum
funding: Admission is free. The museum opened under Chew's Culture Foundation, founded in 1991.

name: MOCA Taipei
funding: Its support page lists the sponsors Thermos, Contemporary Art Foundation, Sony, Epson and Royal Inn.

name: Taipei Contemporary Art Center
funding: Artist-run space founded 2010. In 2013 its director said most money came from sales of donated artworks, plus a small government subsidy (about 15%). No current funder list found.
